column1: # One row per registered OPTION KEY, per POSITIONAL value shape, and per
# KEYWORD spelling. Tab-separated; lines beginning with "#" are comments;
# the first non-comment line is the header row.
# Every `shape` and `accepted_syntax` value below was derived by RUNNING the
# reference parser (editor/figdown.html @ 0.1), not from prose. Where
# a genre document or core.md disagrees with the parser, the row records the
# PARSER and the disagreement is listed in syntax-style.md §10.
# THE `source` COLUMN WAS RE-DERIVED. Every attribution
# below was checked against the PRIMARY source — the standard's own grammar,
# schema or reference text — and the row records the quote or the negative.
# The previous revision was wrong in BOTH directions: it marked ~87 of ~124
# `table`, `cell`, `bitfield` and `gap`, all of which ARE borrowed; and it
# attributed `numbering` and `src`/`dst` to IETF, which no IETF document
# supports. Rows whose attribution moved carry `ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED
# 0.1` in `exception_reason`; rows where the rename moved AWAY from an
# attested spelling say so in capitals (there are exactly two: `plane` and
#   key               row id WITHIN its `kind`; the table's primary key is the
#                     pair (kind, key). SIX spellings appear once as an option
#                     `routing` `width` — which is a fact about the language,
#                     not a duplicate row. `layer` is retired in both
#                     `PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`); all three still occupy two rows apiece, for the
#                     same reason every other retired spelling does — the
#                     engine owes each registration its own named diagnostic.
#                     The line read FIVE and omitted `plane` while the pair was
#                     LIVE, which is when the fact it records was easiest to
#                     Option keys use the bare spelling; a key
#                     that carries two value shapes or two registration kinds
#                     ONE KEYWORD SPELLING CARRIES A GENRE QUALIFIER, and it
#                     is the first: `state` is declared TWICE, by `statechart`
#                     and by `sequence`, and the two are DIFFERENT CONSTRUCTS
#                     under one word (`GENRE-VOCABULARY-OBLIGATION` makes a spelling a per-genre
#                     declaration, never one inherited). The bare `state` row
#                     is `statechart`'s, because that declaration came first
#                     and nothing that cites it moves; the second is
#                     `state.sequence`, split on the same principle as
#                     value shapes, two rows. A row per DECLARATION is what
#                     makes the table checkable: one row could not carry two
#                     grammars, two source clauses and two statuses at once.
#                     A RETIRED spelling keeps its own row, so the table is
#                     also the retirement registry: `layer` appears once as a
#                     retired keyword and once as a retired option key, which
#                     is the same fact about the language the `plane`/`plane=`
#                     pair recorded while it was live — and
#                     records as a WITHDRAWN pair instead.
#                     A WITHDRAWN spelling keeps its row too. 0.1
#                     (`EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`) is the first case and 0.3 (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`) is the
#                     the same terms. `EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`: `path` and `routing` and the
#                     were removed from the language rather than renamed, so
#                     their rows carry status `retired` with NO successor to
#                     point at — the one thing that distinguishes a withdrawal
#                     from every other retirement in this table.
#                     Deleting them was considered and REJECTED, and the reason
#                     is worth having on the record: three of the rows here
#                     attributions as standing precedent, core §10 keeps all six
#                     REGISTERED as retired diagnostics because a registration
#                     counts whether or not it has a live acceptor, and the
#                     engine still owes each one a named diagnostic. A table
#                     that is the retirement registry cannot drop the entries
#                     that make it one. The COUNTS below therefore count LIVE
#                     registrations only, exactly as they did before — a
#                     withdrawn row is present and uncounted, like every retired
#                     §11 promises this file is "the machine-readable half of
#                     the punctuation scheme", and until then that promise held
#                     for KEYS and VALUE SHAPES only: §1 is about MARKS, and
#                     rows at all. A mark row's `key` is the mark's NAME (the
#                     characters themselves are not safe TSV primary keys), its
#                     `source_spelling` is the literal mark, and its
#                     `accepted_syntax` states the mark's ROLE and where it is
#                     ordinary text. Marks are not counted in the option-key or
#                     keyword totals below — they are a fourth namespace, not
#                     more members of the first three.
#   source            the standard the SPELLING is borrowed from:
#                     SVG CSS DOT IETF ISO GFM multimd Mermaid D2 WaveDrom
#                     HTML C ECharts Grafana Highcharts FigDown
#                     (`Mermaid D2 WaveDrom HTML C` extend the enum named in
#                     the style-guide brief; see syntax-style.md §4.1 — the
#                     genre docs cite all five and none is expressible as one
#                     of the eight. `ECharts` was added for the
#                     two chart rows: no member of the older enum has any
#                     charting primitive at all, and recording the chart
#                     vocabulary as coined would have been false.
#                     the two scalar-marker rows: no member of the older enum
#                     has a threshold or a value-band primitive at all, and
#                     both were recorded as coined, which was false in both
#                     cases. FigDown = coined by this project.)
#                     Two VALUE SETS come from standards outside the enum and
#                     are recorded in `conflicts` rather than in `source`,
#                     because the KEY they sit under is coined here:
#                     and `terminator`, taken whole from ISO 5807. Until then
#                     no ISO vocabulary was borrowed, because `shape=` is
#                     purely geometric (`SHAPE-ENUM-VOCABULARY`/`EXTERNAL-EDGE-ENDPOINTS`) and the role vocabulary had
#                     not been designed. ISO 5807's symbol vocabulary is
#                     Process, Decision, Predefined process, Manual operation,
#                     Preparation, Parallel mode, Loop limit, Data, Stored
#                     data, Manual input, Document, Line, Control transfer,
#                     Communication link and Dashed line, plus Terminator
#                     (§9.4.2) — SIXTEEN names, twelve of them stage symbols
#                     and four line symbols. FigDown borrows THREE stage roles
#                     symbol*, read first-hand 2026-08-13 — ISO's own name for
#                     it is "Line"; `VOCABULARY-SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION`), and records the rest as
#                     §Roles, *What is excluded*): the two-word names fail
#                     `GENRE-DOCUMENT-CONTRACT` §6(a), and the media symbols have no corpus demand.
#                     gap, with the measurement that would close each gap) is
#                     THE LIST IS THIS REPOSITORY'S RECORD, NOT A READING of
#                     the standard: it contains no Connector, no Comment and
#                     no Ellipsis row, and whether ISO 5807 defines them is
#                     CORRECTED 0.3.z — THE RECORD IS SHORT, AND THE SHORTFALL
#                     IS INSIDE THE READABLE PAGES. Counted against ISO 5807's
#                     readable pp. 1-8, clause 9 names TWENTY-ONE symbols:
#                     mode, 9.2.2.6 Loop limit) and four line (9.3.1 Line,
#                     9.3.2.3 Dashed line). So the sixteen above OMIT six
#                     access storage, Direct access storage, Card, Punched
#                     tape, Display) and INCLUDE one, Terminator, that sits
#                     past p. 8 and is unread. Seventeen readable stage names,
#                     not twelve; FigDown spells two of them (Process,
#                     Decision), so the stage coverage gap is FIFTEEN.
#                     Nothing about the three borrowed roles changes; the
#                     DENOMINATOR does, and it was chosen by whoever wrote
#                     this record rather than by the standard. Enumeration in
#                     the project’s working record; class analysis in
#                     stay unread, so twenty-one is a FLOOR.
#                     ONE VERIFICATION IS OPEN: ISO 5807 §9.4.2 was not
#                     available (paywall; pp. 1-8 of 25 only), so the spelling
#                     `terminator` rests on draw.io, Visio and secondary
#                     sourcing, against ANSI X3.5-1970 and Mermaid which say
#                     `Terminal`. `Z-ORDER-KEY-NAMING` decides it once the clause is read.
#   source_spelling   how that standard spells it (`-` when coined here)
#                     (`mark` is the shape of every `kind=mark` row and of no
#                     other row: a mark has a ROLE, not a value grammar.)
#                     named in the brief; see syntax-style.md §11.)
#   accepted_syntax   what the parser accepts, as a regex or literal set
#                     every row that carried it has now either been renamed or
#                     ruled to keep its spelling, so the value is gone and no
#                     row may reintroduce it — a scheduled rename is a rename
#                     that has not happened, which is exactly the state this
#                     table exists to make impossible to leave lying around)
#   conflicts         a foreign standard that spells this differently or
#                     means something else by it; `-` if none known
#   exception_reason  NON-EMPTY only where the row breaks a rule stated in
#                     syntax-style.md; names the rule and the release

column6: accepted_syntax
column8: conflicts
column9: exception_reason

column1: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- option keys (46 rows here for 45 distinct spellings; 20 of the 46 are LIVE, `PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`).
# The header read `42 registered` in an earlier release and that figure was already stale: core.md §10 re-derives it row by row and
# records that 0.1 registered `description` (`DESCRIPTION-KEY-SPELLING`) and `present` (`PRESENCE-CONDITION-EXPRESSION`) without recounting — 42 + 2 = 44 distinct keys in 45 rows; 0.1
# registered `index` (`BITFIELD-REPETITION-CONSTRUCT`, the bitfield repetition range), making it 45 distinct keys in 46 rows, the
# two NORMATIVE rows spelled `fill` being ONE key with two registrations. `EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS` changed NO total here: `points` `routing` `tailport`
# `headport` — all four accepted only by the withdrawn `path` — keep their rows with status `retired`, which is the same treatment `via`
# `src` `dst` `w` `h` `dir` `kind` `level` and `text` already get. THIS AGREES WITH core.md §10, deliberately: a registration counts there
# whether or not it has a live acceptor, the engine still owes each spelling a named diagnostic, and a table that doubles as the retirement
# registry cannot drop the entries that make it one. Deleting the four was considered on the ground that this table attributes
# a LIVE spelling to the standard it was borrowed from — and rejected, because three surviving rows (`word`, `pin`, and `via`/`src`/`dst`)
# cite the withdrawn attributions as standing precedent, so deleting them would have left three arguments pointing at nothing. `level`
# stayed registered as a retired diagnostic (figdown.html:321-323); that convention is unchanged and covers all four.
# `PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT` changes NO total here either, for the same reason: `plane` and `z-index` — the option key that referenced a declared plane, and the
# integer accepted by `plane` and by nothing else — move from status `experimental` to status `retired` and keep their rows. What DOES move is the count of
# LIVE keys: 22 live option rows before, 20 after. The two rows are kept because the diagnostics are live and because two OTHER rows point at them — `layer`
# and `z`, whose retirement diagnostics named `plane=` and `z-index=` as their replacements. Both had to be rewritten to state the WHOLE CHAIN
# (`layer=` -> `plane=` -> withdrawn; `z=` -> `z-index=` -> withdrawn), because a rename that names a withdrawn target sends an author to a spelling that is
# itself a line error. That is the `route` -> `path` repair, owed a second time. One live key also LOST an acceptor without changing status:
# `external` took `plane=` and nothing else, so after `PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT` it takes no option key at all.

column6: `(<x>,<y>)` — a PAREN POINT in canvas px, `pin` only; components -?\d+(\.\d+)?. It is the PLACEMENT key of the three the line may carry, not the whole of it: (`ELEMENT-GEOMETRY-DIRECTIVE`) `pin` also takes `width=`/`height=`, and every one of the three is optional (a `pin` with none of them is a line error). `at=` is the one with the WIDER domain — nodes, groups and `external` endpoints alike; the extent keys are nodes only. The bare comma pair was retired (RULE 1.1a).
column8: DOT spells node position `pos=` (neato/fdp only); CSS basic shapes use the WORD `at` to introduce a position (`circle() = circle(<radial-size>? [ at <position> ]?)`) but never as a key. Verified negative in Graphviz's 176 attributes, the SVG 1.1/2 attribute indexes, D2's keyword table and Mermaid.

column6: \d+(\.\d+)?% in [0,100], the `%` is MANDATORY; `threshold` only. Renamed from `at=` (`TEXT-COLOUR-KEY-NAMING` family) so no key carries two value shapes. The host directive was spelled `guide` until 0.1 (`THRESHOLD-KEYWORD-SPELLING`).
column8: SVG's `offset` is on `<stop>` (gradient position) and on `feFunc*` (gamma constant); there is NO `offset` on `<mpath>`/`<animateMotion>`. CSS's positional analogue is `offset-distance`.

column8: CSS/HTML `class` — same meaning, aligned

column6: #rgb | #rrggbb | one of 147 lowercase CSS colour names | transparent (figdown.html:143)

RETIRED on `edge` `threshold` `bundle` (`INTERIOR-LESS-ELEMENT-PAINT`): no interior, so `fill=` and `stroke=` named one channel and `stroke=` won silently. Line error naming `stroke=`. A CLASS that sets `fill=` with no `stroke=` and is used by an edge is a line error too.

same value set as `fill`. NORMATIVE (`STROKE-KEY-STATUS`): it is the OUTLINE of anything with an interior and the WHOLE of a line (`edge`, `bundle` ring, `threshold`) — SVG's own asymmetry (`<rect stroke>` vs `<line stroke>`), corroborated by mxGraph `strokeColor`, D2 `style.stroke` ("applies to shapes and connections") and Mermaid `linkStyle … stroke:`. `CONSTRUCT-STATUS-TIERS` had demoted it on 5 in-repo uses; re-measured at 56+ in-repo and 567 downstream edge-colouring sites.

RETIRED 0.1 (`TEXT-COLOUR-KEY-NAMING`): renamed to `color=`, which 0.1 retired in turn (`COLOUR-KEY-STATUS`). v0.1 has NO label-colour key; the default is derived from the background's WCAG relative luminance (core §5, `LABEL-COLOUR-SOURCE`).

solid | dashed | dotted, BARE — a quoted value is a line error (RULE 2.4, `RULE-POSITION-ENUMERATION`). Acceptors: node (incl. process/decision/terminator) group edge bundle threshold band class. `field` `cell` `signal` LOST the key (`STYLE-KEY-SCOPE`) — on a field it could erase the dash that is `optional`'s only carrier while the model kept the flag, which is `PRESENTATION-AS-MEANING-CARRIER`'s prohibition.
column8: DOT's `style` is a COMMA LIST mixing stroke, fill and visibility (`filled` `invis` `rounded` `striped` …); FigDown narrows it to the line-style members. HTML/SVG `style` is inline CSS. CSS's true line-style enum is `border-style` (`<line-style> = none|hidden|dotted|dashed|solid|double|groove|ridge|inset|outset`).
column9: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 0.1: was `FigDown`. Graphviz documents the values verbatim — "For nodes and edges: dashed dotted solid invis bold".

column6: <group-id> on `node` (containment) · <node-or-group-id> on `threshold`/`band` (annotation target)
column8: SVG's filter-primitive `in` ("Identifies input for the given filter primitive") is an unrelated homonym; D2 has no `in`.
column9: DECLARED EXCEPTION (§8.1): one key, two relations; kept because the relations are disjoint per directive. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 0.1: was `FigDown`. Mermaid architecture-beta: `group private_api(cloud)[Private API] in public_api`.

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic. Was the id of a declared `plane`. Spelled `layer=` until 0.1 (`PLANE-KEYWORD-SPELLING`); WITHDRAWN with the `plane` keyword (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), so the diagnostic names NO replacement spelling. `external` had this as its ONLY option key and now takes none at all.
column8: COINED, and the near-concept is attested elsewhere under `layer` with INCOMPATIBLE semantics: mxGraph makes a layer a containment PARENT establishing coordinates, Inkscape layers are `<g>` and may carry a transform, OGC WMS requires an `<SRS>` per layer, Graphviz layers are separate OUTPUT OVERLAYS, CSS `@layer` is cascade priority. SVG has no layer at all.
column9: RENAME AWAY FROM AN ATTESTED SPELLING (`PLANE-KEYWORD-SPELLING`) — the one place this table records a move from a borrowed word to a coined one. Accepted because every attestation carries a different meaning; see requirements-notes `PLANE-KEYWORD-SPELLING` for the objection. WITHDRAWN (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`): a keyword and its only declaration point move together, so the key went with `plane` for the same reason it was demoted with it. The whole `layer=` -> `plane=` -> withdrawn chain is now stated in the `layer` row's diagnostic, because naming `plane=` alone would send an author to a spelling that is itself a line error.

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic. Renamed `plane=` (`PLANE-KEYWORD-SPELLING`); `plane=` was itself WITHDRAWN (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`) with the `plane` keyword, so the message states the WHOLE CHAIN, `layer=` -> `plane=` -> withdrawn, and names NO live replacement. The correct action is to DELETE the line.
column8: Graphviz `layer` = "Specifies layers in which the node, edge or cluster is present", an OUTPUT OVERLAY, not a paint plane
column9: RETIREMENT CHAIN REPAIRED 0.3 (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), the `route` -> `path` precedent.

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic. Was `-?\d+` integer on `plane` and on nothing else. Spelled `z=` until 0.1 (`Z-ORDER-KEY-NAMING`); WITHDRAWN with its only host directive `plane` (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), so the diagnostic names NO replacement spelling.
column9: MISSING ROW ADDED 0.1 — the live key had no row while its retired predecessor did. WITHDRAWN 0.3 (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`), the `points=`/`tailport=`/`headport=` treatment: an option key accepted by exactly one directive goes when that directive goes. CSS's `z-index` is unaffected as an attestation and the row keeps it, because the `z` row's diagnostic cites it.

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic. RETIRED 0.1 (`Z-ORDER-KEY-NAMING`): renamed to `z-index=`, CSS's spelling taken in full (RULE 4.2) — and `z-index=` was itself WITHDRAWN (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`) with its only host directive `plane`. The message must state the WHOLE CHAIN, `z` -> `z-index` -> withdrawn, because naming `z-index=` alone sends an author to a spelling that is now a line error. The correct action is to DELETE the line.
column9: RETIREMENT CHAIN REPAIRED 0.3 (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`). The precedent is `route` -> `path`, where the same repair was owed when a rename's target was withdrawn under it.

column8: the `timing` CHILD KEYWORD `gap <cycle>` is a different concept (timing.md:128-134); namespaces disjoint

column6: box | rounded | circle | ellipse | diamond | cylinder, BARE — a quoted value is a line error (RULE 2.4, `RULE-POSITION-ENUMERATION`) ; `cloud` retired 0.1 with a named diagnostic (figdown.html:123)
column8: Mermaid carries role on bracket shape — rejected here (`SHAPE-ENUM-VOCABULARY`/`EXTERNAL-EDGE-ENDPOINTS`). DOT's `shape=` is the same key for the same concept and supplies `box` `ellipse` `circle` `diamond` `cylinder` verbatim.
column9: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 0.1: was `FigDown`. ONE value is NOT DOT's: `rounded` is a DOT *style* ("causes the polygonal corners to be smoothed"), written `shape=box, style=rounded`; FigDown coined it as a shape.

column6: \d+ >= 1 ; absent -> 32 (figdown.html:1291). Spelled `unit=` until 0.1 (`BITS-PER-ROW-KEY-NAMING`).
column8: Mermaid names the identical setting `bitsPerRow`: semantically exact, and it stays rejected because core §10 makes LOWERCASE ASCII a conformance invariant, not because camelCase is a style preference — the same invariant already decided ECharts `bar3D` -> `bar3d`, mxGraph `exitX`/`exitY` -> DOT `tailport`/`headport`, and mxGraph `edgeStyle` -> `routing`, so taking `bitsPerRow` would cost the invariant plus the standing of those three. THE LAST TWO OF THOSE THREE ARE NOW HISTORICAL PRECEDENTS (`EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`): `tailport=`/`headport=`/`routing=` were withdrawn from the language with the `path` directive and no longer have rows in this table. That does NOT weaken the argument, and the citations are kept rather than deleted for exactly that reason: a precedent is a decision the invariant once made, and the invariant made all three. What the withdrawal removes is a live row to point at, not the fact that camelCase was refused three times on this ground. packetdiag (blockdiag/nwdiag) spells it `colwidth` (`colwidth = 32` in its TCP/IPv4 examples): REJECTED — it collides TWICE inside FigDown, with the live `width=` (a px extent) and with `table`'s `width` child keyword (per-column widths), so `colwidth=32` reads as "columns are 32 px wide" — a legal, WRONG figure with nothing to warn on (`PAINT-KEY-NAMING` §1's inverted prior) — and it would reinstate the `colw` abbreviation removed. bytefield-svg spells it `boxes-per-row` ("how many boxes are drawn on a row before moving to the next row"): the hyphen would be legal (a source may hyphenate; `z-index` is the precedent), but the UNIT is BOXES, not bits — borrowing a spelling while changing the counted thing is the `gap.tick` mis-borrow this table already retired once. WaveDrom bitfield's `bits` is a FIELD's width per item and "overall bitwidth" as a CLI flag, never bits-per-row — a reverse collision.
column9: The NOUN is IETF's (RFC 2360 §3.1 "each word horizontal on the page"; RFC 791 §3.1 counts the header in "32 bit words"). No standard defines a KEY named `word` or `unit` for this. FOUR identifier attestations of the setting exist and all four are rejected above (Mermaid `bitsPerRow`, packetdiag `colwidth`, bytefield-svg `boxes-per-row`, and the reverse-colliding WaveDrom `bits`); the 0.1 audit knew only the first, and its claim that it was "the only identifier attestation anywhere" was FALSE — corrected 0.1 (`BITFIELD-GENRE-NAMING`). KEPT BY DEFAULT, NOT BY MERIT: `word` is a prose noun lifted from RFC 791/2360, not a key any source defines, so under `SIZE-AND-DIRECTION-KEY-NAMING`'s own logic it is a coinage wearing borrowed clothes, and it is the rare coinage that asserts something checkably FALSE for ~20 of ~217 corpus instances (`word=15` is a correct row width and no architecture's word). It survives because every attested alternative is worse. REOPEN when either holds: (a) a source spells this setting as ONE lowercase word with no FigDown collision, or spells it hyphenated in BITS; (b) the corpus's non-word widths pass roughly 25-30%, making the false connotation the common case — at which point the reopened question is the lowercase-ASCII invariant itself, deliberately, not a bitfield patch. NB RFC 791 Appendix B does NOT contain the word.

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic -> `word=` (`BITS-PER-ROW-KEY-NAMING`)
column8: C's "unit" is the addressable STORAGE unit (packing), not the row width; `unit=32` also reads as "the unit is 32", inverting count-vs-unit

column6: lsb0 | msb0, BARE — a quoted value is a line error (RULE 2.4, `RULE-POSITION-ENUMERATION`). REQUIRED on every `bitfield`, no default (figdown.html:1308)
column8: The VALUES `lsb0`/`msb0` are Accellera SystemRDL 2.0's, verbatim (Table 26: "msb0 — Specifies register bit-fields in an address map are defined as 0:N versus N:0"; "lsb0 — … This is the default"). IEEE 1685/IP-XACT has no bit-order property at all (only `endianness`, which is BYTE order).
column9: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 0.1: was `IETF`, which is FALSE — `lsb0`, `msb0` and `numbering` appear ZERO times in RFC 791, RFC 1700, RFC 8174 and draft-mcquistin-augmented-ascii-diagrams-13 (which never became an RFC). RFC 2360's only hit is the prose "bit numbering at the top". The KEY is coined here; the VALUE SET is SystemRDL's.

column6: quoted prose; acceptors node process decision terminator state group edge flowline transition title; requires figdown 0.3 (OPT_MIN_VERSION); refused on field with a named diagnostic; DRAWS (a folded-corner note box, `DOMAIN-CONVENTION-DIRECTIVES` places it)
column8: PARTIAL BORROW, declared. The METACLASS is UML 2.5.1's `Comment`, not `Note` — so the word is not taken whole from one standard and RULE 4.1 is only half satisfied. What IS borrowed whole is the NOTATION: the symbol that metaclass draws is the NOTE SYMBOL, and that is what every diagram tool calls it — PlantUML `note left of Alice`, Mermaid `Note over A,B`, GFM `> [!NOTE]`. So `note` is borrowed, not coined: the picture is UML's Comment and the spelling is its notation's. Recorded as "partial" rather than claiming a whole borrow, because a later reader checking RULE 4.1 against UML's metaclass list would not find it. `comment=` was BARRED (FigDown already calls `#` a comment and `MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE` fixes that a comment is never parsed, so one word would mean both "never rendered, never parsed" and "always rendered"); `callout=` was REJECTED as attested in no standard. ISO 5807:1985 §9.4.3 DEFINES an annotation symbol (reached via §9.3.2.3 *Dashed line*, which cross-references it as the symbol surrounding "an annotated area"), read first-hand from the published preview 2026-08-13. That is a source for the CONSTRUCT in flowchart's own standard and is NOT a source for the spelling: the symbol's NAME is past page 8 and is unread, so nothing here should be read as ISO endorsing the word `note`. Recorded because it strengthens RULE 4.1's construct case while leaving the borrow partial.
column9: REVIVED AS A LIVE OPTION KEY 0.3 (`DRAWN-ANNOTATION-FORM`), under SYNTAX-STYLE RULE 4.9. It was retired (`DESCRIPTION-KEY-SPELLING`) IN ORDER TO RESERVE THIS NAME — the retirement diagnostic and core §10 both said so — and it retired BEFORE v0.1.0 shipped, so no published document ever carried the old meaning and the reader RULE 4.3 guards against cannot exist. This cashes a stated reservation; it does not reverse a decision. The old spelling meant `description=` (machine-facing prose, no ink); the new one is the DRAWN annotation, and the two keys now divide by AUDIENCE. Under figdown 0.1/0.2 the key is a line error naming 0.3, because accepting it there would repaint an author's tooltip as ink.

column6: one token or a quoted string (`QUOTING-RULES`: quoted, because the delimiter is whitespace); acceptor: `field` only. Spelled `note=` until 0.1 (`DESCRIPTION-KEY-SPELLING`).
column8: SystemRDL spells the same property `desc`: REJECTED by RULE 4.2 (an option key takes the primary source's spelling IN FULL; no standard abbreviates this one twice over). IP-XACT/IEEE 1685-2022 spells it `description`, and so do DocBook, Doxygen (`\description`) and JSON Schema.
column9: AUTHORED DOCUMENTATION PROSE, and it produces NO INK beyond an SVG <title> tooltip. A fact a human must SEE belongs in the label or in a `class` meaning. On §12.7's MAY-conclude list: quotable and displayable, never parsable.

column8: `labels` appears NOWHERE in WaveDrom's schema or WaveJSON reference; `data` is its own key — "Is an array of signal labels. Each value slot of signal lane can be labeled using this field."
column9: §2.2: quoting does NOT protect a comma — `data="a,b"` is TWO elements; no label may contain a comma. Fixed 0.1

column6: no acceptor; named diagnostic -> `data=` (`SIGNAL-DATA-KEY-SPELLING`)

THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §15.3.14 FOR THE SAME VOCABULARY ("A transition is a directed relationship between a source vertex and a target vertex"), which is what satisfies RULE 4.1's ISO preference; 2.5.1 is the working text because it is NEWER (19505-2 is UML 2.4.1), and that is the WHOLE of the reason. CORRECTED 0.3.z: this cell used to read "deliberately NOT ISO/IEC 19505, which is PAYWALLED and is the older 2.4.1", and the paywall half was FALSE and is withdrawn — ISO/IEC 19505-1:2012 and 19505-2:2012 are free of charge, OMG hosts the normative text at omg.org/spec/UML/ISO/19505-2/PDF, and it has now been fetched and read (decisions/registry.md). The ISO storefront copy is priced; the text is not, and the priced storefront was mistaken for an unobtainable document without anyone opening it. The cell also paraphrased 2.5.1 using 19505's wording ("directed relationship"), which belongs to the 2.4.1 clause quoted above; both are now quoted verbatim against their own edition. Same defect class as `VOCABULARY-SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION` — see decisions/registry.md.

column9: Source is OMG UML 2.5.1 clause 17 (Interactions) — the SINGLE standard every `sequence` word comes from (never mix sources for one genre). Semantics §17.3.3.1, notation §17.3.4.1, metaclass description §17.12.17.1. THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §14.3.17 FOR THE SAME VOCABULARY, which is what satisfies RULE 4.1's ISO preference — clause 14 of that edition IS Interactions, and its Foreword states the text is identical with the OMG specification for UML v2.4.1 Part 2; 2.5.1 is the working text because it is NEWER and complete, and that is the WHOLE of the reason (the `transition` row's pattern). WHOLE BORROW, no verification debt: the clause was read first-hand for decisions/registry.md.

column6: `message <a> [tail] <op> [head] <b> ["label"]`; genre `sequence` ONLY (`SEQUENCE-GENRE-VOCABULARY`). This genre's CONNECTOR spelling, the fourth after `edge`, `flowline` and `transition`; it REPLACES `edge` here. Two differences from every other connector: the operator set is `->` `<-` `<->` and **`--` is a LINE ERROR**, and the grammar adds ONE trailing positional, the quoted message label. A message lands in its own model collection with its source line, because it has a place in the figure's total order and an edge has no position at all. Option keys `class` `stroke` `style` `in` `note` `description`; `fill=` is the interiorless-line error. 0.4.
column8: DOT and FigDown-before-0.4 spell the connector `edge`; ITU-T Z.120 §4.3 defines a message as a relation between an output and an input, so the CONCEPT is the same in both candidate standards and only UML's is borrowed; Mermaid and D2 write the operator with no keyword. THE LABEL HAS TWO SPELLINGS AND ONE MODEL FIELD — the trailing quoted string and the shared scanner's inline `-[mid]->` position both reach it, writing both on one line is a line error, and the design record settles the trailing form while saying nothing about the brackets. That is an ALIAS in `IDENTITY-ASSERTION`'s sense and is FILED, not ruled, in genres/experimental/sequence.md.
column9: Source is OMG UML 2.5.1 clause 17, the same single standard as `lifeline`. Notation §17.4.4.1, metaclass description §17.12.18.1. THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §14.3.18 FOR THE SAME VOCABULARY (RULE 4.1's ISO preference), with 2.5.1 as the working text for the edition reason above. WHOLE BORROW, verified. The `--` refusal rests on the same clause family: §17.4.3.1 defines the LOST case as the one where the receiving event occurrence is absent, so a Message ordinarily carries BOTH a sending and a receiving occurrence and one with unstated direction is not a thing this domain has.

column6: `state <lifeline-id> "<state name>"`; genre `sequence` ONLY (`SEQUENCE-GENRE-VOCABULARY`). A SECOND declaration of the `state` spelling, not the `state` row inherited: slot 1 REFERENCES a declared `lifeline` and declares NOTHING (nothing in this genre refers to a state occurrence, so it takes no id of its own), where `statechart`'s slot 1 DECLARES an id. Slot 2 is MANDATORY — a state occurrence with no name asserts nothing. Two CONSECUTIVE `state` lines naming the same lifeline and the same name are a line error. Option keys `class` `fill` `stroke` `style` `in` `note` `description` — the language's FIRST genre-conditional option row, because `shape=`, `width=` and `height=` name nothing on a construct with no shape and no extent of its own. 0.4.
column8: The COLLISION is with FigDown's own `state` under `statechart` (see that row): same spelling, same value grammar in slot 2, DIFFERENT slot 1 and a different source clause. Admitted under `GENRE-NAMESPACE` `GENRE-VOCABULARY-OBLIGATION`, and the genre document must state the asymmetry in the sentence that introduces the keyword — it does. ITU-T Z.120 §4.7 spells the same construct `condition` and would have been the better word had Z.120 won the source choice; Mermaid has no construct for it at all.
column9: PARTIAL BORROW, DECLARED. The spelling is clause 17's OWN NOTATION PROSE, not the metaclass name and not a cross-reference into §14: OMG UML 2.5.1 §17.2.4.5 reads "The state symbol represents the equivalent of a constraint that checks the state of the object represented by the Lifeline". The metaclass is `StateInvariant` (§17.12.25), and Table 17.1 (§17.8.1.1) lists the state symbol as a graphic node of sequence diagrams. THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §14.3.25 FOR THE SAME VOCABULARY (RULE 4.1's ISO preference). Recorded the way the `note` row is recorded: the picture is UML's metaclass, the spelling is its notation's. The same clause also confirms that this construct belongs INSIDE the interaction — UML makes the link to a state machine a should-match naming convention, not a binding — which is why the genre needs no reference to a `statechart` document and why a reader may not bind the two.

column6: `fragment <id> ["label"] type=<operator>` — genre `sequence` ONLY (`SEQUENCE-GENRE-VOCABULARY`). `type=` is MANDATORY (see the `type.fragment` row). Declares an id in the document-wide namespace. Members are named by `in=` and MUST be CONTIGUOUS in declaration order; nesting is capped at ONE level for v1, on the v0.1 `group` precedent, and that cap is a SCOPE decision rather than a principle. No `fill=`: a fragment is a FRAME over the messages it holds and painting its interior would hide them. 0.4.
column8: Nothing in FigDown competes for the spelling. `group` was REFUSED for this genre (`SEQUENCE-PARTICIPANT-GROUPING`) and is NOT this construct's neighbour: a fragment frames a RUN OF OCCURRENCES, a group would have banded a set of PARTICIPANTS, and UML clause 17 has no construct for the second. Mermaid and PlantUML open the block with the operator itself and have no keyword for the container.
column9: PARTIAL BORROW, AND THE DEBT IS LARGER THAN A HEAD-NOUN REDUCTION — recorded here in those words rather than smoothed over (`VOCABULARY-SOURCE-ATTRIBUTION`: prefer a weaker verifiable claim to a stronger false one). In OMG UML 2.5.1, `fragment` ALONE already names something and it is not this construct: §17.12.13 `InteractionFragment` is "an abstract notion of the most general interaction unit", `CombinedFragment` (§17.12.3) is ONE subclass of it, and so are `StateInvariant` (§17.12.25.1), OccurrenceSpecification and InteractionUse. So under this genre a `state` line IS a fragment in the source's sense while not being a `fragment` in FigDown's, and a reader checking RULE 4.1 against the metaclass list finds the word at the WRONG LEVEL OF THE HIERARCHY. THE WORD IS KEPT ANYWAY, and the alternatives are named: UML's own spelling is a compound, barred by RULE 4.5b's no-compounding corollary; ITU-T Z.120's is *inline expression*, two words, barred by `GENRE-DOCUMENT-CONTRACT` §6(a); neither Mermaid nor PlantUML has one. `fragment` is attested STANDALONE in the source's own clause title (§17.6 *Fragments*) and in its prose. THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §14.3.3 FOR THE SAME CLASS (RULE 4.1's ISO preference).

column6: `operand <id> ["guard"] in=<fragment-id>` — genre `sequence` ONLY (`SEQUENCE-GENRE-VOCABULARY`). `in=` is MANDATORY and its object is a FRAGMENT, never another operand: a compartment of a fragment has no meaning apart from one, and has no compartments of its own. The quoted string is the GUARD. Declares an id in the document-wide namespace. No `fill=`, for the same reason as `fragment`. 0.4.
column8: Nothing in FigDown competes for the spelling. THE COINAGE THAT LOST: this construct was proposed as `branch` and reversed at `FRAGMENT-OPERAND-SPELLING`, because `branch` is a coinage AGAINST BOTH candidate standards — which is the thing RULE 4.1's letter exists to stop. The objection on record, that `operand` reads as arithmetic, is an UNMEASURED READABILITY CLAIM and `START-STATE-KEYWORD` refuses exactly those; the `plot` -> `chart` precedent does not reach it either, because `plot` was refused for reading as an IMPERATIVE and `operand` commands nothing (`PAINT-KEY-NAMING` §1 ranks *opaque* strictly better than *inverted*). REOPENS AGAINST `operand` on a measured misreading rate at the bar `decision` cleared — 22% over 216 nodes — and on nothing weaker.
column9: WHOLE BORROW, verified, and BOTH candidate standards say it. OMG UML 2.5.1 §17.12.14 `InteractionOperand`: "An InteractionOperand is contained in a CombinedFragment. An InteractionOperand represents one operand of the expression given by the enclosing CombinedFragment." Notation §17.6.4.1: "InteractionOperands are separated by a dashed horizontal line. The InteractionOperands together make up the framed CombinedFragment." ITU-T Z.120 §7.2 writes `<operand area>` throughout its grammar. THE CITATION IS ISO/IEC 19505-2:2012 §14.3.14 FOR THE SAME CLASS (RULE 4.1's ISO preference), with 2.5.1 as the working text. Taking the NOUN from the same enumeration whose twelve ADJECTIVES this genre already takes under RULE 4.2 is also the consistent position.

column6: declares a semantic class; meaning REQUIRED. Where it properly belongs — nearer `LAYOUT-ZONE-NAMESPACE`'s genre-independent namespace than `GENRE-VOCABULARY-OBLIGATION` — is an open question `SUBJECT-VOCABULARY-SCOPE` does not settle.

column6: `threshold "<label>" in=<node|group> offset=<0..100>%`; the label is mandatory and quoted, the `%` is mandatory. NO `value=` and NO `ref=` (`THRESHOLD-VALUE-SCOPE`): zero corpus figures carry a literal numeric value — every reference is a named software-configurable register, and the name already lives in the label. DECLARED BY `block` ONLY (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`): `topology`, `flowchart` and `statechart` withdrew it on zero authored uses and on a reason each genre supplies for itself — a threshold is drawn at a percentage of the target's RENDERED EXTENT, and a state box, a process box and a router glyph are all sized by their label, so the line asserts nothing a reader can read.
column8: VERIFIED against Grafana's own docs: the feature is called "thresholds" and its "Show thresholds" option offers "As lines", "As filled regions" and "As filled regions and lines" — FigDown's marker + region pair, split the same way. SECONDARY: IETF RED/AQM — RFC 2309 says "Two RED parameters, minth (minimum threshold) and maxth (maximum threshold)", and RFC 7567 "an AQM algorithm configured with a threshold"; this is exactly what the corpus's WRED figures transcribe. `level` was rejected on three collisions (downstream `_LEVEL`/`_LVL` registers mean a profile INDEX; the corpus's threshold tables head the ordinal column `Level (high → low)` and the value column `Threshold`; ISO 80000-3 defines level as the LOGARITHM of a quantity ratio). `watermark` was rejected on coverage.
column9: DELIBERATELY UNFROZEN (`GENRE-EARNING-THRESHOLD`): held as the interim general construct for a future scalar-marker genre, which is why it was NOT renamed — renaming now would hand that genre a retired word. NOTE THE IRONY, recorded because a reader will meet it: in the QoS domain the secondary source cites, a threshold is a queue depth WITH A NUMERIC VALUE (RFC 2309 `minth`/`maxth`, RFC 7567), while FigDown's takes no `value=` (`THRESHOLD-VALUE-SCOPE`) and its `offset=` is a fraction of the target's rendered extent, not a quantity of anything.

The label became MANDATORY and quoted (`BAND-LABEL-STATUS`); the RANGE separator moved off the hyphen onto `..` (`RANGE-SPELLING`) and this cell said `<a>-<b>%` until 0.1. Spelled `fill` until 0.1. DECLARED BY `block` ONLY (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`).
column8: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 0.1: was `FigDown`. VERIFIED against the Highcharts API reference — `plotBands` is "An array of colored bands stretching across the plot area marking an interval on the axis", and its sibling `plotLines` is "An array of lines stretching across the plot area, marking a specific value on one of the axes": ONE vocabulary supplying the same marker + region pair FigDown has. Tableau corroborates with "Reference Lines, Bands, Distributions, and Boxes". Grafana names the region half "filled regions" rather than a band, which is why `threshold` is sourced there and `band` here. IN `topology`'s OWN DOMAIN the word is taken by the FREQUENCY BAND, which is why that genre withdrew it rather than carry a caveat. It does NOT collide that way in `block`, because `block` has no single domain — that is what general-purpose means — and the same word being safe in one genre and misleading in another is itself the argument for per-genre declaration (core §1, `GENRE-VOCABULARY-OBLIGATION`; `SUBJECT-VOCABULARY-SCOPE`).
column9: `fill` is now a RETIRED keyword and a LIVE option key — the declared `UNSAFE-DEFAULT-ELIMINATION` exception (core.md §10) DELIBERATELY UNFROZEN (`GENRE-EARNING-THRESHOLD`), like `threshold`: not renamed for the same reason.

column6: the ring is derived. DECLARED BY `topology` ONLY (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`): `block` withdrew it on ZERO authored uses — every authored link bundle in the corpus is a topology document — and `flowchart`/`statechart` withdrew it as an anti-feature, since two flowlines between one pair of stages are different CONDITIONS and two transitions between one pair of states are different TRIGGERS.
column8: verified negative as a keyword everywhere checked; DOT's `group` attribute description contains "for bundling edges" — a concept cousin under a different spelling. THE REFERENT IS IEEE 802.1AX: a Link Aggregation Group, and by extension an ECMP set and an EVPN Ethernet Segment. That standard's own noun is `aggregation`, which FigDown does NOT take.
column9: RULE 4.1 EXCEPTION, DECLARED 0.3 (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`). `topology` defines this construct BY ITS REFERENT — IEEE 802.1AX LAG — but cannot take the standard's noun whole, because `aggregation` is FALSE for two of the three things the construct covers: an ECMP set is not an aggregation and neither is an EVPN Ethernet Segment. `bundle` is kept as the umbrella spelling over all three. This is the shape RULE 4.1 requires of a mix: name the primary source, show it cannot express the need, and draw the line. Under `block` the construct had NO referent to name and its definition had to be geometric, which is the divergence the pre-R159 shared text hid.

column9: COINED — see the `plane` OPTION row for the five incompatible attestations of `layer`. WITHDRAWN, not renamed (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`): the second exercise of the withdrawal power after `EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`'s `path`/`routing`, and the same shape. The correct action on a `plane` line is to DELETE it, and the measurement says that costs nothing: stripping the declared plane and its `plane=` from `examples/evpn-fabric.fd` leaves an SVG of the same 12449 bytes, one differing token out of 198 (`data-edge="36"` -> `data-edge="35"`), because the overlay's whole visual identity came from `class=overlay`. The implicit `planes[0] = {id:"base", z:0}` is UNAFFECTED and stays NORMATIVE (core §12.2); paint order is document order. The row is KEPT — the convention `path` `routing` `via` `src` `dst` `size` `boundary` sit under — because the diagnostic is live and the negative attestation is the evidence other rows cite.

FigDown deliberately does NOT follow C for the container, because `struct`/`structure` is disqualified above. Two sources, one for the figure and one for the member, is the `GENRE-DOCUMENT-CONTRACT` §6(e) split: a genre is named after the FIGURE KIND, a construct after the thing it is.

column1: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- lexical marks (10 rows). syntax-style.md §1 is the prose half; these are the machine-readable half of it,
# and until 0.1 they did not exist — §11 promised the TSV covered the punctuation scheme, and the promise held for keys and value shapes only. A mark row is NOT counted in the option-key
# or keyword totals above: marks are a fourth namespace. The five §1 STRUCTURAL marks are `comma` `parens` `brackets` `quote` `semicolon`; `hash` `backslash` `range-dots` `colspan` `rowspan`
# are the residual marks §1 assigns to a specific construct's value grammar, and the last four were missing from §1's own residual list until this release.

column6: SEPARATES THE ELEMENTS OF A LIST — always, everywhere (SYNTAX-STYLE §1). One job in 12 positions, audited whole. A comma-delimited list is ONE whitespace-free token (RULE 3.2); a QUOTED element protects its own comma (`LINK-OPERATOR-IN-IDS`). Ordinary text inside a quoted string, an `[edge label]`, a comment and a GFM pipe row.
column8: CSS, JSON and GFM all trim whitespace around a comma; FigDown does NOT, because a positional list must terminate at whitespace for the rest of the line to stay reservable (RULE 3.1).

column6: GROUPS A COMPOSITE VALUE (a point or a tuple) so it can be ONE element of a list — `at=(x,y)`, `cell (h1,2)` (RULE 1.1a). Not a call, not a precedence group; FigDown has no expressions.

VERBATIM TEXT REGION — the label slot inside an edge operator, `-[mid]->`. Balanced brackets nest verbatim; `["…"]` takes the standard escapes for unbalanced brackets and `\n`. `;` has been ordinary text inside it (`SEMICOLON-STATUS`) and `#` (`VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE`). Earned its row in SYNTAX-STYLE §1.

STRING LITERAL: it delimits AND it enables escapes. WHERE it is required, forbidden or inert is RULE 2's four-way answer (core §1): mandatory at whitespace-delimited string positions, a LINE ERROR at id, enum and bare-flag positions, INERT at number/point/percentage/range positions. Ordinary text only via `\"`.

RESERVED for a future statement separator (C/C++-like) and MUST NOT be given any other meaning (RULE 1.3, core §1). A line error wherever a processor is reading grammar, with a diagnostic naming the reservation (`SEMICOLON-STATUS`). Ordinary text in all four verbatim regions: quoted string, `[edge label]`, comment, GFM pipe row.

COMMENT introducer, at line start or after whitespace — which is what keeps `fill=#0d9488` a colour. Ordinary text in the same four verbatim regions as `;`; the `[edge label]` half landed (`VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE`), before which `edge a -[hop #1]-> b` was `unterminated [label]`.
column8: `#` introduces a comment in shell, Python, YAML and TOML — aligned; it is a fragment identifier in URLs and a heading in Markdown, neither of which appears in a FigDown directive.

column6: ESCAPE INTRODUCER, and it exists in exactly two disjoint places: inside a quoted string, where `\n` `\"` `\\` are the ONLY escapes (any other is a line error); and inside a GFM pipe cell, where `\|` and `\^^` are the ONLY escapes and every other backslash — `\n` included — is literal cell text (`TABLE-CELL-BACKSLASH`). Added to SYNTAX-STYLE §1's residual list.
column8: C, JSON and GFM all use `\` as the escape introducer — aligned; GFM escapes any ASCII punctuation, FigDown escapes a closed set.

column6: THE LANGUAGE'S ONE RANGE SEPARATOR, inclusive at both ends (RULE 4.8, `RANGE-SPELLING`): `index=0..7`, `band "X" 15..35%`. EXACTLY two dots — a longer dot run is a line error. Added to SYNTAX-STYLE §1's residual list.
column8: Ada ISO/IEC 8652 `1 .. 10`, Pascal ISO 7185 `array [1..10]`, X.680 `SIZE(1..4)` — all inclusive, all attested. Rust and Python spell an EXCLUSIVE range with two/one dots, which is the conflict the inclusive choice is measured against.

column6: A DIGRAPH, not two `|`. In a pipe row a cell whose RAW segment is EMPTY — zero characters between the two pipes — merges LEFT. A whitespace-only segment is an ordinary empty cell: the encoding is INJECTIVE and both readings are goldens. **The mark an author types is therefore the ABSENCE of characters**, which is why a formatter that pads cells rewrites the figure — core §9 `COLSPAN-EMPTY-CELL-SPELLING`, filed. Added to SYNTAX-STYLE §1's residual list in the same release.
column8: multimd's own alternative spelling for a span is an explicit token; GFM has no span at all.
column9: `TABLE-ROW-SYNTAX` ADOPTED this spelling and, in the same paragraph, REJECTED whitespace-as-alignment because "formatters like Prettier pad cells arbitrarily" and "invisible characters carrying semantics is a classic failure mode". Both arguments apply to the adopted rule; filed as core §9 `COLSPAN-EMPTY-CELL-SPELLING` rather than fixed, because the genre is frozen.

column6: A DIGRAPH, not two `^`. A pipe cell that is EXACTLY `^^` merges UP; `\^^` is a literal caret pair. It may not appear in the first header row, nor in the first data row (rowspan does not cross the delimiter row, `MERGE-ACROSS-DELIMITER-ROW`), and a merge must form a rectangle (`TYPED-BLOCK-SILENT-FALLBACK`). Added to SYNTAX-STYLE §1's residual list.
